note: Ixekizumab binds no rodent IL-17A, so the class went to psoriasis patients on patient-derived cells, a keratinocyte gene set, cynomolgus toxicology and human IL-17 genetics; no psoriasis animal model was in the chain.
label: Psoriasis (IL-17A)

engagement.model: Primary human keratinocytes stimulated with IL-17 and TNF (synergistic gene set)
engagement.note: IL-17 plus TNF synergistically induced 160 keratinocyte genes that track the psoriasis lesion signature; the paper predicts IL-17 antagonists will modulate them most.
engagement.quote: Our data predict that psoriasis therapy with either TNF or IL-17 antagonists will produce greater modulation of the synergistic/additive gene set, which consists of the most highly expressed genes in psoriasis skin lesions.
engagement.judgement: Year is the online date (epub 2010-11-18); print 2011. Chosen as the engagement model because the first ixekizumab mechanistic study read out exactly this gene set.

engagement.model: Primary human keratinocytes stimulated with IL-17 and TNF (synergistic gene set)
engagement.note: In ixekizumab-dosed patients' lesions the IL-17/TNF synergistic gene set fell by 2 weeks, more than in earlier TNF-antagonist studies, as the keratinocyte model predicted.
engagement.short: Lesional IL-17 gene set fell by week 2
engagement.quote: The effect of IL-17 blockade on expression of genes synergistically regulated by IL-17 and TNF-α was of higher magnitude at 2 weeks than in prior studies with TNF-α antagonism.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed); full text in PMC3470466 not read.
engagement.reason: Lesional gene set fell as predicted
engagement.judgement: Called a stated comparison: the paper reads out the in vitro synergistic gene set from Chiricozzi 2011 (shared senior author) in dosed patients. Readout is IL-17-induced keratinocyte transcripts, so downstream. Phase 1 trial NCT number not given in the abstract; registry_date not found.
engagement.magnitude_basis: lesional mRNA of the IL-17/TNF synergistic gene set

engagement.confidence_note: Report date of bTDR08 not given; year is the IND opening (2007-11-01) as proxy.
engagement.note: Human IL-17A injected into C57BL/6 mice raises plasma KC (mouse CXCL1); ixekizumab blocked it (sponsor report bTDR08), the filed in-vivo engagement test.
engagement.short: Ixekizumab blocks hIL-17A-induced KC in mice
engagement.quote: Ixekizumab administration decreased hIL-17 induced KC secretion in C57BL/6NHsd mice (Report bTDR08).
engagement.judgement: Opened at the IND date as the proxy for first use, as the draft does for the other filed ixekizumab studies. Izokibep was later run in the same challenge model (Klint 2023).
engagement.model: Mice injected with human IL-17A, plasma KC (CXCL1) readout

engagement.magnitude_basis: mouse plasma KC after hIL-17A challenge vs lesional CXCL1 mRNA in patients
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read via PMC (PMC3470466). Phase 1 NCT number not given in the paper; registry_date not found.
engagement.note: In ixekizumab-dosed patients' lesions CXCL1 and IL-8, the human homologues of the mouse KC readout, fell more than 6-fold by week 2. Retrodiction: the mouse result was first public in the 2016 FDA review, after ixekizumab's 2012 lesional result for the same target.
engagement.quote: As illustrated in Figure 3, genes that were strongly suppressed (change >6-fold) by ixekizumab included: IL-19, a potent inducer of epidermal hyperplasia; IL-8 and CXCL1, known IL-17 induced chemokines with potent ability to attract neutrophils
engagement.reason: CXCL1 fell in patients as in mice
engagement.judgement: A pairing: the mouse result became public only in the 2015 FDA review (posted 2016), so the entry is dated 2016. Mouse readout is induced plasma KC; human readout is lesional CXCL1 mRNA, the same chemokine but a different compartment and no exogenous challenge, so downstream, not direct. Re-scored retro under the post-dating rule: engagement is a target claim, and the patient result (Krueger 2012) was public before the model's first public statement (FDA review 2016), whatever the 2007 run date.
engagement.model: Mice injected with human IL-17A, plasma KC (CXCL1) readout

dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology (only cross-reactive species)
dose.note: Ixekizumab binds human and monkey but not mouse or rat IL-17A, so cynomolgus carried the 9-month toxicology; NOAEL 5 mg/kg/week. IND opened November 2007.
dose.short: Cynomolgus is the only tox species
dose.quote: Based on the injection site reactions requiring dose suspension, the NOAEL for this 9-month study was 5 mg/kg/week.
dose.judgement: Year is the IND submission date (2007-11-01, FDA clinical review) as a proxy for first use; the review itself is dated 2015-11-02 and was posted with the 2016 approval.

dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology (only cross-reactive species)
dose.note: Patients got the full regimen (160 mg then 80 mg, ≤2.67 mg/kg) under the 5 mg/kg/week NOAEL; injection-site reactions, the monkey's limiting toxicity, were mostly mild and stopped no one. Retrodiction: the margin was first public in the 2015 FDA review, after ixekizumab's own Phase 2 patient results (2012).
dose.short: Cyno NOAEL margin held at clinical dose
dose.quote: Most injection site reactions were mild-to-moderate in severity and did not lead to discontinuation of TALTZ.
dose.judgement: Paired by me: the review states the NOAEL and the maximum human dose (2.67 mg/kg) but does not set them against patient outcomes. Injection-site reactions occurred at 17% vs 3% placebo, below the monkey margin, but were not dose-limiting, so not scored as a toxicity block. No animal efficacy exposure target exists: the clinical dose came from the Phase 2 dose range, so only the tolerability end is scored (decision 16). Re-scored retro under the post-dating rule (settles the checker's decision-16 question: the public date governs, not the filing date): dose is a drug claim, and ixekizumab's own Phase 2 dosing and tolerability (Leonardi 2012) were public before the NOAEL's first public statement.
dose.magnitude_basis: monkey NOAEL 5 mg/kg/week vs maximum human dose 2.67 mg/kg

dose.confidence_note: Year is the EudraCT registration (2015-004531-13) as proxy for the toxicology programme; the 26-week study may have completed later.
dose.note: Izokibep binds monkey but not rodent IL-17A; 26-week monkey NOAEL 20 mg/kg/week (human equivalent 6.5 mg/kg, 520 mg), limited by an injection-site abscess at 40.
dose.quote: due to the formation of local abscess and systemic sequelae that were considered as adverse event (AE) in one female administered 40 mg/kg/week, the NOAEL was determined to be 20 mg/kg/week
dose.judgement: A separate track from the draft's cyno-tox-ixekizumab because dose is split by modality and this is the protein (Affibody) member's own study.
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology of izokibep (only cross-reactive species)

dose.magnitude_basis: monkey NOAEL 20 mg/kg/week (HED 6.5 mg/kg) vs highest Phase 2 dose 160 mg q2w
dose.note: Patients took up to 160 mg every 2 weeks (about 1 mg/kg/week, under the 6.5 mg/kg human-equivalent NOAEL); harms matched placebo apart from mild injection-site reactions. Retrodiction: the monkey margin was first public in Klint 2023, after izokibep's own Phase 2 psoriasis result was announced as tolerable (press release 2020-06-15).
dose.short: Margin held at the effective dose
dose.quote: During the placebo-controlled period, AEs in the izokibep groups were similar to placebo except for mild injection site reactions.
dose.judgement: Paired by me: the effective dose (80-160 mg every 2 weeks, Phase 2) sits about 6-fold under the monkey NOAEL's human equivalent per week. The monkey's limiting harm was an injection-site abscess; patients had only mild injection-site reactions, so no toxicity block. AFFIRM-35 (NCT03591887) has no registry results. Re-scored retro under the post-dating rule: dose is a drug claim, and Affibody's 2020-06-15 AFFIRM-35 top-line release ('Overall, ABY-035 treatment appeared tolerable and safe.') was public before the NOAEL's first public statement (Klint 2023).
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology of izokibep (only cross-reactive species)

efficacy.model: Psoriasis patients' blood cells ex vivo (IL-17-secreting cells, sponsor report bTDR80)
efficacy.note: Sponsor's psoriasis rationale: patient blood held more IL-17-secreting cells than healthy donors'; the only filed animal efficacy work was surrogate antibodies in arthritis and EAE mice.
efficacy.quote: Thus neutralization of IL-17 may be an effective treatment for psoriasis.
efficacy.confidence_note: Report date of bTDR80 not given; year is the IND opening (2007-11-01) as proxy.
efficacy.judgement: Chose the patient ex-vivo study over the filed surrogate-antibody CIA and EAE mouse models, because it is the only filed system that made a psoriasis prediction; ixekizumab does not bind rodent IL-17A, and no psoriasis animal model was filed.

efficacy.model: Psoriasis patients' blood cells ex vivo (IL-17-secreting cells, sponsor report bTDR80)
efficacy.note: Ixekizumab Phase 2: PASI 75 at week 12 in 77-83% on 25-150 mg vs 7.7% placebo, the primary endpoint, as the IL-17 rationale predicted. Retrodiction: the model data were first public in 2016, after IL-17A blockade had already worked in psoriasis patients (2012).
efficacy.quote: At 12 weeks, the percentage of patients with a reduction in the PASI score by at least 75% was significantly greater with ixekizumab (except with the lowest, 10-mg dose)--150 mg (82.1%), 75 mg (82.8%), and 25 mg (76.7%)--than with placebo
efficacy.judgement: A pairing: the trial (2012) precedes public release of the model data (FDA review posted 2016), so the entry is dated 2016, when both sides were public. Quote is the first 40 words of a longer sentence. Prediction is direction only. Leonardi registry results posted 2017-07-25. Re-scored retro under the post-dating rule: efficacy is a target claim; Leonardi 2012 was public before the model's first public statement in the 2016 FDA review.

patient_trials.quote: UNCOVER-1 ixekizumab Phase 3 in plaque psoriasis; registry results posted 2016-05-27 (results not read here).
At week 12, PASI 90 response rates were 0%, 5%, 19%, 71% and 59% for the placebo, 2-, 20-, 80- and 160-mg izokibep groups, respectively.

efficacy.confidence_note: Exact date of the mouse study not given; year is the first-in-human start (NCT02690142, 2016-02) as proxy, since the paper places it in preclinical development.
efficacy.note: Izokibep was run in the same hIL-17A/KC mouse model before first-in-human dosing (2016) and called 30- to 50-fold more effective than the antibodies.
efficacy.short: Mouse KC model: izokibep beats mAbs
efficacy.quote: On an mg/kg basis, izokibep provided 30- and 50-fold superior efficacy in reducing KC secretion relative to ixekizumab and secukinumab, respectively.
efficacy.judgement: The paper calls its in-vitro and in-vivo work 'preclinical psoriasis models' and claims superior efficacy, so the model made a psoriasis efficacy prediction for izokibep, which ixekizumab's filing did not.
efficacy.model: Mice injected with human IL-17A, plasma KC (CXCL1) readout

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Model side read in full (PMC10187109).
efficacy.note: Izokibep Phase 2 met its primary endpoint, PASI 90 at week 12: 71% on 80 mg vs 0% placebo. The predicted edge over ixekizumab was not tested head to head. Retrodiction: the izokibep mouse data were first public in 2023, after IL-17A antibodies had worked in psoriasis (2012) and after izokibep's own top-line result (press release 2020-06-15).
efficacy.quote: At week 12, PASI 90 response rates were 0%, 5%, 19%, 71% and 59% for the placebo, 2-, 20-, 80- and 160-mg izokibep groups, respectively.
efficacy.judgement: Scored on direction (izokibep works in psoriasis). The model's magnitude claim, 30-fold better than ixekizumab, has no head-to-head test; across trials izokibep's 71% PASI 90 is close to ixekizumab's Phase 3 rates, so the superiority looks over-stated, but that is my cross-trial reading and not scored. AFFIRM-35 (NCT03591887) has no registry results. Re-scored retro under the post-dating rule: efficacy is a target claim and IL-17A neutralization had shown psoriasis efficacy since 2012 (ixekizumab), before the model's first public statement (Klint 2023). Affibody announced AFFIRM-35 top-line PASI 90 71% on 2020-06-15 (press release via FirstWord), also before the model side; year stays 2023, when both sides were public.
efficacy.model: Mice injected with human IL-17A, plasma KC (CXCL1) readout

safety.model: People with inborn errors of IL-17 immunity (IL-17RA, IL-17F deficiency)
safety.note: Patients lacking IL-17RA or IL-17F had chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis and little else, predicting Candida as the class's on-target harm.
safety.quote: These experiments of nature indicate that human IL-17A and IL-17F are essential for mucocutaneous immunity against C. albicans, but otherwise largely redundant.
safety.judgement: The FDA clinical review cites this paper as the basis for the Candida expectation. Epub 2011-02-24.

safety.model: People with inborn errors of IL-17 immunity (IL-17RA, IL-17F deficiency)
safety.note: FDA review sets the genetic prediction beside the trials: Candida infections 1.4% on ixekizumab every 2 weeks vs 0.5% placebo; oral candidiasis 0.7% vs 0.
safety.short: Candida rose as IL-17 genetics predicted
safety.quote: suggest that blockade of IL-17 increases the risk for fungal infections, particularly mucocutaneous candidiasis, as well as staphylococcal skin infections (including abscesses).
safety.judgement: Quote is the closing clause of a sentence that begins with the human genetic observations. Inflammatory bowel disease, the other on-target harm on the label, was not scored: no filed model predicted it, and healthy cynomolgus in a 9-month study (the filed model) could not show a 0.1-0.2% exacerbation of pre-existing disease.
